(a) the energy of combustion of a compound is the sum of the energies of combustion, per mole of compound, of all of the atoms present in the molecule, plus the energy of combustion, per gram, of the hydrogen present as a component of the hydrocarbon skeleton, and (b) the energy of formation, per gram,of the hydrogen component of the hydrocarbonskeleton is 0.1305 kcal/g.

the standard enthalpy of formation of a substance can be calculated from the energy of combustion of the substance and the standard enthalpies of combustion of the elements from which the substance is formed, provided that the energy of combustion is measured by rotating-bomb calorimetry, and that the standard entropies of combustion of the element are known with sufficient accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of heats of combustion of organic substances in a rotating bomb calorimeter.
the determination of standard heats of combustion of organic compounds, using a bomb calorimeter of the rotating-bomb type (see Figure 1).
the determination of the standard heats of combustion of organic compounds, and with the calculation of standard heats of formation from these heats of combustion.

, although the accuracy of combustion calorimetry has been improved, and although new techniques have been developed, there has been no major advance in the determination of the heats of formation of organic compounds.
the combustion calorimetric determination of standard enthalpies of organic compounds is now a well-established technique.

the calorimetry of combustion has now reached an unprecedented degree of accuracy, and is now capable of yielding values for standard heats of formation for organic compounds which have an accuracy of about 0.1% or better, and which are in most cases comparable in accuracy with values of the entropy of formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to determine the energies of combustion, and hence the standard heats offormation, of organic compounds to within ±0.1 per cent of the true value.
we have made some progress in the direction of achieving Professor Rossini's object, but we are still a long way from achieving it.
we have made progress, but not spectacular progress, in the calorimetry of combustion reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now measure the heats of combustion of a wide variety of compounds, including some containing the elements S and Si.
we are able to determine the standard enthalpy of formation of organic compounds with an accuracy of about 0.2 kJ/mol.
